messages.author: 26c971075f8aedcc
messages.subject: Standardizing observed values
parts:
Hei,

Up to now I have been running INLA mainly with artificial datasets with more or less standardized variables. I wonder how default prior specifications in INLA work with arbitrary scale of data. Say I have some observed values (y) coming from N(100, 9) and I want to infer some model parameters, say a simple linear regression on x (y = a + bx + e). Is it ok to:
A) run INLA directly on "raw" y or
B) should I standardize y first and then transform marginals (for a and b) to match the "raw" scale of y

Thanks!

Regards, Gregor

> some observed values (y) coming from N(100, 9) and I want to infer

> + e). Is it ok to:
> A) run INLA directly on "raw" y or
> B) should I standardize y first and then transform marginals (for a
> and b) to match the "raw" scale of y

the default priors in inla are fixed and do not consider the scale of
the input.

messages.subject: Odg.: Re: [r-inla] Standardizing observed values
parts:
Tnx for the prompt reply!

I tested the behaviour using the example bellow. It seems that I get more or less the same results if I standardize y or not even for N(100, 3), which is quite of from "normal", i.e. N(0, 1). I have been running some models with fixed variances and I got trapped by my own mistake of not scaling that parameter two, which lead me to the initial question. Bellow is an example that shows what I have been fiddling with.

N.B. recently submitted summary.inla.marginal returns NA for SD, because inla.emarginal still does not work for vectors.

gg

---

library(package="INLA")

n     <- 100
mu    <- 100
b     <-  1
x     <-  runif(n, min=-1, max=1) * 10
eta   <- mu + b*x
sigma <- 3
y     <- rnorm(n, mean=eta, sd=sigma)
hist(y)

data <- list(y=y, x=x)

formula <- y ~ 1 + x
result <- inla(formula, family="gaussian", data=data)
summary(result)

## Fixed effects:
##                  mean         sd 0.025quant  0.5quant 0.975quant          kld
## (Intercept) 99.706086 0.33902820 99.0393748 99.706071 100.372013 3.697785e-32
## x            1.016441 0.06000464  0.8984381  1.016439   1.134303 0.000000e+00
## Model hyperparameters:
##                                         mean    sd      0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant
## Precision for the Gaussian observations 0.09119 0.01272 0.06840    0.09048  0.11827

data$yS <- (data$y - mu ) / sigma
formulaS <- yS ~ 1 + x
resultS <- inla(formulaS, family="gaussian", data=data)
summary(resultS)

## Fixed effects:
##                    mean         sd 0.025quant    0.5quant 0.975quant kld
## (Intercept) -0.09796953 0.11303802 -0.3202645 -0.09797383  0.1240614   0
## x            0.33881461 0.02000649  0.2994707  0.33881394  0.3781117   0
## Model hyperparameters:
##                                         mean   sd     0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant
## Precision for the Gaussian observations 0.8200 0.1146 0.6155     0.8132   1.0649

marginal.mu <- inla.tmarginal(fun=function(x) (x * sigma) + mu, marginal=resultS$marginals.fixed$'(Intercept)')
marginal.b  <- inla.tmarginal(fun=function(x) (x * sigma),      marginal=resultS$marginals.fixed$x)

inla.marginal.summary <- function(x, ...)
{
  ## x - marginal as defined in ?inla.emarginal
  ## ... - other arguments
  m1 <- inla.emarginal(fun=function(z) z,   marginal=x, ...)
  m2 <- inla.emarginal(fun=function(z) z^2, marginal=x, ...)
  s  <- sqrt(m2 - m1^2)
  q  <- inla.qmarginal(p=c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), marginal=x, ...)
  c(mean=m1, sd=s, "0.025quant"=q[1], "0.5quant"=q[2], "0.975quant"=q[3])
}
  
inla.marginal.summary(marginal.mu)
##       mean          sd  0.025quant    0.5quant  0.975quant 
## 99.7060910   0.3391141  99.0384939  99.7040911 100.3696893
## 99.706086    0.3390282  99.0393748  99.7060710 100.3720130 from raw scale
inla.marginal.summary(marginal.b)
##       mean         sd 0.025quant   0.5quant 0.975quant 
## 1.01644375 0.06001948 0.89828610 1.01609006 1.13389351
## 1.016441   0.06000464 0.8984381  1.016439   1.134303   from raw scale

## --> we get the same results if we run INLA on: A) "raw" values or B) standardized y and rescale marginals back to "raw" scale

data$yS <- (data$y - mu ) / sigma
formulaS <- yS ~ 1 + x
resultS2 <- inla(formulaS, family="gaussian", data=data, control.data=list(initial=log(1/(sigma^2)), fixed=TRUE), inla.call=inlaCall,)
summary(resultS2)
## Fixed effects:
##                   mean         sd 0.025quant    0.5quant 0.975quant kld
## (Intercept) -0.0979703 0.30569756 -0.6983138 -0.09798029  0.5015313   0
## x            0.3388138 0.05410525  0.2325593  0.33881199  0.4449192   0
## The model has no hyperparameters

marginal.mu <- inla.tmarginal(fun=function(x) (x * sigma) + mu, marginal=resultS2$marginals.fixed$'(Intercept)')
marginal.b  <- inla.tmarginal(fun=function(x) (x * sigma),      marginal=resultS2$marginals.fixed$x)
  
inla.marginal.summary(marginal.mu)
##        mean          sd  0.025quant    0.5quant  0.975quant 
##  99.7060891   0.9170926  97.9032252  99.7006834 101.4981416
##  99.706086    0.3390282  99.0393748  99.7060710 100.3720130 from raw scale
inla.marginal.summary(marginal.b)
##       mean         sd 0.025quant   0.5quant 0.975quant 
##  1.0164413  0.1623157  0.6973533  1.0154845  1.3336157
## 1.016441   0.06000464 0.8984381  1.016439   1.134303   from raw scale

## --> however, this is not the case when variances are being fixe as we need to scale variance as well

resultS3 <- inla(formulaS, family="gaussian", data=data, control.data=list(initial=log(1/((sigma/sigma)^2)), fixed=TRUE), inla.call=inlaCall,)
summary(resultS3)
## Fixed effects:
##                   mean         sd 0.025quant    0.5quant 0.975quant kld
## (Intercept) -0.0979703 0.30569756 -0.6983138 -0.09798029  0.5015313   0
## x            0.3388138 0.05410525  0.2325593  0.33881199  0.4449192   0
## The model has no hyperparameters

marginal.mu <- inla.tmarginal(fun=function(x) (x * sigma) + mu, marginal=resultS3$marginals.fixed$'(Intercept)')
marginal.b  <- inla.tmarginal(fun=function(x) (x * sigma),      marginal=resultS3$marginals.fixed$x)
  
inla.marginal.summary(marginal.mu)
##       mean          sd  0.025quant    0.5quant  0.975quant 
## 99.7060920   0.3056998  99.1051330  99.7042901 100.3034471
## 99.706086    0.3390282  99.0393748  99.7060710 100.3720130 from raw scale
inla.marginal.summary(marginal.b)
##       mean         sd 0.025quant   0.5quant 0.975quant 
## 1.01644392 0.05410571 0.91008037 1.01612499 1.12216962
## 1.016441   0.06000464 0.8984381  1.016439   1.134303   from raw scale

## --> now we are closer, but there is some underestimation of posterior standard deviation
